title: Two Truths and a Lie
intro: Three statements per round: two are true, one is not. Tap the one you think is the lie. Nothing is saved; it is all in this tab.

statements.text: I have shipped production mobile apps with real users and store releases.
I wrote my first compiler pass before I turned twelve.
I still enjoy pairing with juniors when there is time on the calendar.
I treat accessibility regressions like production incidents.
I have never broken a CI pipeline on a Friday.
I prefer small PRs with screenshots over giant theory threads.
Teaching forced me to explain tradeoffs I used to hand-wave.
I only work in greenfield codebases with zero legacy.
Game jams are where I test ideas that later become talks or demos.

outcomes.message: Right call. The lie was the odd one out; the other two lines are grounded in real work.
Not that one. Try another statement.
You cleared every round. Thanks for playing.
